text.p: Defence electronics group Thomson-CSF said in a statement it expected a profit in 1996 after three years of losses.
"The net result should become positive again due to the disappearance of the negative effects related to, these last three years, the stake in Credit Lyonnais," the company said in a statement.
Thomson-CSF has a 18.92 percent stake in the state-bank, and Thomson SA another three percent, as a result of the sale for shares of its Altus finance unit.
Losses at the bank weighed on Thomson-CSF which made losses of respectively 791 million, 962 million and 2.305 billion in the past three years.
Thomson-CSF reported its first half net attributable profit was slightly higher at 396 million francs, from 364 million in the first half of last year.
Sales were up 5.9 percent to 16.43 billion francs.
Thomson-CSF said its order book stood at 68.28 billion francs at June 1996, representing 22 months of sales, against 70.94 billion at December 1995.
"For the year as a whole, the sales figure should be slightly higher than that of the previous year due to international sales," it said.
It added that it expected an operating result in line with the first half at about five percent of sales.
On October 16, the French government said it planned to sell Thomson SA to Lagardere Groupe which plans to buy-out Thomson-CSF minorities.
Thomson-CSF said it was appointing an expert to advise the board on the Lagadere buy-out offer so that it could give an opinion to shareholders when needed.
